APA-formatted correlation table

Source: R/tables.R
apa_cor.Rd

APA-formatted correlation table

Usage

apa_cor(
  data,
  note = NULL,
  p_value = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  digits = 2,
  bold_significant = FALSE,
  star_significant = TRUE,
  significance_note = TRUE,
  output = c("flextable", "tibble"),
  font_family = NULL,
  font_size = NULL,
  text_color = "black",
  border_color = "black",
  border_width = 0.5,
  line_spacing = NULL,
  table_width = 1,
  keep_empty_star_columns = TRUE,
  summary_functions = list(M = mean, SD = stats::sd),
  column_formats = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

data.frame or tibble with variables to be correlated, or the output of correlation::correlation() (see Details)

note

Custom note to appear below table. (Overrides automatic note.)

p_value

p-value needed to be flagged as significant

digits

Number of digits for rounding

bold_significant

bold significant correlations

star_significant

start significant correlations

significance_note

If TRUE, place note at bottom of table that significant correlations are bolded.

output

output type. Can be "flextable" or "tibble"

font_family

font family

font_size

font size, in points. If NULL (default), the size set with apa7_defaults(font_size = ) (12 unless changed).

text_color

text color

border_color

border color

border_width

border width in pixels

line_spacing

spacing between lines of the header and body (e.g., 2 for double spacing or 1 for single spacing). If NULL (default), the spacing set with apa7_defaults(line_spacing = ) (2 unless changed). Table notes are single-spaced.

table_width

proportion of the width of the page that the table occupies, from 0 to 1: 1 (default) is the full width, and .5 is half the width. The column widths are scaled to fill this proportion of the width of the text area, which is 6.5 inches (letter-size paper with 1-inch margins) unless changed with apa7_defaults(page_width = ). With 0, the column widths are left as they are. In apa7 0.2.0 and earlier, table_width was a width in inches; values greater than 1 are still read as inches, with a warning.

keep_empty_star_columns

Keep remove empty star columns (Default: TRUE)

summary_functions

Any named list of functions that summarize data columns (e.g., list(Mean = mean, SD = sd)). Can also be a character vector of function names (e.g., c("n", "M", "SD")). Functions available in a character vector: IQR, Interquartile Range, Kurtosis, MAD, Median Absolute Deviation, M, Mean, Med, Median, n, N, Quantile, Range, SD, Skewness, Var, Variance

column_formats

column_formats object

...

<data-masking> parameters passed to psych::corTest (not used for correlation::correlation() output)

Value

flextable::flextable

Details

By default, apa_cor() computes Pearson correlations with psych::corTest(), and the stars are for unadjusted p-values.

For other kinds of correlations (e.g., Spearman, Kendall, robust, or partial correlations), compute them with correlation::correlation() and pass the result as data. The table shows its correlations and p-values, and the summary columns are computed from the data that correlation::correlation() keeps with its results. The note says what kind of correlations are shown (unless they are ordinary Pearson correlations) and how the p-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons: correlation::correlation() uses Holm's method by default, so the stars are for adjusted p-values unless p_adjust = "none". Correlations computed by group, between two sets of variables, or with Bayesian methods are not yet supported.

# Spearman correlations from the correlation package
if (requireNamespace("correlation", quietly = TRUE)) {
  correlation::correlation(trees, method = "spearman") |>
    apa_cor()
}
